h1: The 5 Best Tablets Under $150 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 tablets under $150 scored on screen resolution, real RAM, storage and battery, from the Fire HD 10 to budget Android 15 slates.
summary: The Amazon Fire HD 10 is the pick if you care about the screen: a true 1080p panel on 4GB of RAM. The URAO 10.1-inch gives you Android 16, 128GB and a 6000mAh battery for a little less. The ECOPAD is the most storage-friendly Android 15 slate, the NOVOJOY bundles a stylus and case, and the HOTTABLET 7-inch is a small kid-sized option.
intro: Budget tablet listings love big numbers: 12GB of RAM, 128GB of storage, Android 16. Read the small print and half of that RAM is virtual memory borrowed from storage, which does nothing for speed. The number that matters is physical RAM, and the number nobody advertises is screen resolution, since a cheap 1280x800 panel looks soft next to a 1080p one.

We ranked five tablets that sit entirely below $150 by price bucket, so the Evermyth, which is listed in the $100 to $200 band, was excluded. Each was scored on the Primea framework with the most weight on physical RAM, display resolution, storage and battery. We could only rate what the listings state, and we flag where a tablet's claims lean on virtual memory.

products.name: Amazon Fire HD 10 Tablet
products.verdict: A real 10.1 inch 1080p screen, 4GB of RAM and a 13 hour battery. The best screen in the group.
products.description:
The Fire HD 10 has a 10.1 inch Full HD (1080p) display, an octa-core processor, 4GB of RAM, 32GB of storage and up to 13 hours of battery life. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It wins on the specs that cannot be faked. The 1080p panel is sharper than every 1280x800 rival here, and 4GB of physical RAM is what the others try to make up with virtual memory. Compared with the URAO, you get a better display but lose storage: 32GB is a quarter of the URAO's 128GB. It also runs Fire OS rather than stock Android, so the app store is narrower.

Buy it for streaming, reading and family use. The limits are the 32GB base storage and the Amazon-flavored software, so plan on a memory card if you hoard downloads.
cons: Fire OS has a narrower app store
products.idealFor: Streaming, reading and shared family use.
products.skipIf: You need stock Android and lots of local storage.

products.name: URAO 10.1-Inch Android 16 Tablet
products.verdict: Android 16, 128GB and a 6000mAh battery in the $50 to $100 bucket.
products.description:
URAO ships Android 16 on a 1.8 GHz octa-core processor, with 6GB of RAM plus 30GB of virtual memory, 128GB of storage that can grow to 1TB with a TF card, a 6000mAh battery, dual cameras and a low blue light screen.

Its storage is the story. Four times the Fire HD 10's space, plus a card slot, makes it the better choice for downloaded video and offline reading. It ranks second because the listing does not state a resolution, and the 30GB virtual figure is a marketing add-on, so count only the 6GB of real RAM. Against the ECOPAD it has a newer Android release.

Buy it for a user who wants stock Android and room for files. The unstated display resolution is the gap, so check it before ordering.
products.idealFor: Users who want stock Android and plenty of local storage.

products.name: ECOPAD 10.1-Inch Android 15 Tablet
products.verdict: Android 15, 64GB, cameras and a 1280x800 IPS screen. Half the storage of the URAO.
products.description:
ECOPAD runs Android 15 with 12GB of RAM, of which only 4GB is physical and 8GB is expanded, 64GB of storage with SD expansion to 1TB, a 2MP front and 8MP rear camera and a 10.1 inch 1280x800 IPS display.

The headline 12GB is mostly virtual, so read it as 4GB, the same as the Fire HD 10. It ranks below the URAO because it has less storage and an older Android release, and below the Fire because its 1280x800 panel is softer than 1080p. The listed cameras are the part most budget tablets skip, which helps for video calls.

Buy it for a second family tablet used for calls and browsing. Do not count on the 12GB figure for gaming.
products.idealFor: A second family tablet for calls and browsing.
products.skipIf: You plan to game or multitask heavily.

products.name: NOVOJOY 10-Inch Android 15 Tablet with Case
products.verdict: A stylus and folding case in the box, with 8GB of RAM but only 32GB of storage.
products.description:
NOVOJOY pairs Android 15 and a quad-core processor with 8GB of RAM, 32GB of ROM expandable to 1TB, a 6000mAh battery and a 10.1 inch 1280x800 IPS screen. A stylus and folding case are included.

The bundle is the draw for students and kids, because a case and stylus would add to the cost of the others. It ranks fourth because the quad-core chip is a step down from the octa-core processors in the Fire HD 10 and URAO, and because the listing does not say how much of the 8GB is physical. The 32GB storage matches the Fire but needs a card sooner.

Buy it for a child or a student who will use the stylus. If speed matters, step up to the URAO, since a quad-core chip will be slower.
products.idealFor: Students and kids who benefit from the case and stylus.

products.name: HOTTABLET 7-Inch Android 14 Tablet
products.verdict: A 7 inch kid-sized tablet with a case included, but a 1024x600 screen.
products.description:
The HOTTABLET is a 7 inch Android 14 tablet with a 1024x600 IPS screen, 8GB of RAM of which 3GB is physical and 5GB expanded, 32GB of storage, dual-band Wi-Fi and a protective case in the box. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, the cheapest here.

It ranks last because 1024x600 is the lowest resolution in the ranking and 3GB of real RAM is the thinnest. But its 7 inch size is the only one here that fits small hands or a bag easily. Compared with the NOVOJOY, it costs less but also gives you a smaller, lower-resolution screen.

Buy it for a young child or as a simple e-reader. Anyone who plans to stream or run several apps should step up.
products.skipIf: You want to stream or multitask.

methodology.title: Display resolution
methodology.description: We compared stated panel resolution and size, since a 1080p screen reads far better than 1280x800 or 1024x600.

methodology.title: Physical RAM
methodology.description: Only physical RAM counted toward performance, with virtual memory treated as a marketing figure.

methodology.title: Storage and expansion
methodology.description: Built-in storage and card slot capacity were weighed against how much media a household keeps offline.

methodology.title: Battery
methodology.description: Stated mAh and hours were compared where given, favoring tablets with a quoted runtime.

methodology.title: Price bucket
methodology.description: Only tablets listed entirely under $150 qualified, and features were judged within that limit.

whatMatters.detail: Resolution is the number of pixels on the panel, and on a 10 inch screen it decides how crisp text and video look. A 1080p screen like the Fire HD 10's is noticeably sharper than 1280x800. Look for the resolution in the screen line of the spec list, and treat a missing figure as a reason to ask questions.

Physical RAM is the memory chip, while virtual RAM borrows storage space and is much slower. A tablet listed as 12GB may have only 4GB of real memory, as the ECOPAD shows. Read the breakdown in the memory line, such as 4GB plus 8GB expanded, and judge performance on the first number alone, since the expanded figure only borrows from your storage.

Storage fills quickly with apps, video and photos, and a card slot lets you extend it cheaply. The URAO has 128GB and takes a TF card up to 1TB, while the Fire HD 10 offers 32GB. Check the base figure and the maximum card size on the listing, since a tablet with no slot is stuck.

Fire OS and stock Android behave differently. Fire OS ties you to Amazon's app store, which may lack some apps, while Android 14, 15 or 16 usually offers the broader Play ecosystem. Find the operating system in the spec list, and also check how many update years the maker promises, as budget brands often say nothing.

Battery capacity is in mAh, and hours of use depend on the screen and chip. The URAO and NOVOJOY list 6000mAh, and the Fire HD 10 quotes up to 13 hours. Look for a stated runtime, which is the more useful number, and treat a bare mAh figure as only a rough guide, since a bright 10 inch screen can drain a battery faster than the number suggests.

howToChoose.intro: Start with what you will look at most.

cards.label: Fire OS
cards.text: Built for Amazon content and simple controls, with a smaller app catalog. Pick: Amazon Fire HD 10 Tablet.

cards.label: Android
cards.text: Opens the full Play store and tends to give more storage and cards. Picks: URAO, ECOPAD, NOVOJOY and HOTTABLET.

howToChoose.note: Default to the Fire HD 10 for media, and move to Android if you need specific apps.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A protective case, a manageable size and enough storage for downloaded shows. A card slot lets you add space cheaply.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The NOVOJOY for its case and stylus at 10 inches, or the HOTTABLET for a small 7 inch screen with a case in the box.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need a sharper screen or smooth multitasking. Move above the $150 ceiling, because nothing here pairs 1080p with large storage.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The tablet is for reading or a child. The HOTTABLET is the lowest bucket and still comes with a case.

faq.a: The Android models, including the URAO and ECOPAD, are stock Android and typically run Google apps. The Fire HD 10 runs Fire OS, which uses Amazon's app store instead and may lack some titles.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with budget tablets?
faq.a: Trusting the RAM figure. The ECOPAD lists 12GB but only 4GB is physical, and the HOTTABLET has 3GB of real RAM. Compare the physical number only, where the Fire HD 10 offers a true 4GB.

faq.q: Is the Fire HD 10 worth it over the URAO?
faq.a: If you value the screen, yes. The Fire has a 1080p panel and a quoted 13 hour battery, while the URAO has 128GB, Android 16 and a card slot. Choose by screen or storage.
Use the card slot. The URAO takes a TF card up to 1TB, the ECOPAD an SD card to 1TB and the NOVOJOY expands to 1TB as well. Choose a fast card and format it in the tablet.

faq.q: Do these need maintenance or updates?
faq.a: Update the system when prompted and clear cached app data now and then. The listings state no update promise, so budget Android models like the NOVOJOY may receive few patches. Keep the system updated whenever a patch appears.

Yes, with care. The NOVOJOY and HOTTABLET both include a case, and parental controls exist on Android and Fire OS. A 7 inch HOTTABLET is easier for small hands, while a 10.1 inch screen suits older children.

finalTake: For most buyers the Amazon Fire HD 10 is the best tablet under $150, thanks to its 1080p screen and 4GB of real RAM. If you want Android and more space, choose the URAO with 128GB and a card slot. The ECOPAD suits calls and browsing, the NOVOJOY suits students, and the HOTTABLET fits young children.
